text: Yvy'ape'áripegua atyguasu, oporomarandúmava inglés ha japonés-pe, omyasãima apopyrã español, italiano ha coreano ta'ãngambyry, internet ha tembiporumỹime g̃uarã.
eng_text: Already reporting in English and Japanese, the global organization is launching Spanish, Italian, and Korean-language programs, for television, the web, and mobile devices.

text: Ha’etépe katu ndojehúi cheve nba’eve, hakatu ahecha heta mba’e vai, tapichakuéra ojokaséramo ovetã osẽ hagHa’etépe katu ndojehúi cheve nba’eve, hakatu ahecha heta mba’e vai, tapichakuéra ojokaséramo ovetã osẽ hag̃ua.
eng_text: "Luckily nothing happened to me, but I saw a macabre scene, as people tried to break windows in order to get out.

text: Tapichakuéra ombota apykápe umi vidrio, hakatu ko’ãva ojeka’ỹva ra’e.
eng_text: People were hitting the panes with chairs, but the windows were unbreakable.

text: “Hasypeve, peteĩ vidrio ojeka ha osẽjoa tapichakuéra ovetã rupi”, he’i Franciszek Kowal, tapicha oikovéva.
eng_text: One of the panes finally broke, and they started to get out by the window," said survivor Franciszek Kowal.

text: Mbyjakuéra omimbi ha haku upe energía opoíva rupi, umi átomo hidrogeno ojoaju rupi omoheñói hagMbyjakuéra omimbi ha haku upe energía opoíva rupi, umi átomo hidrogeno ojoaju rupi omoheñói hag̃ua elemento ipohyivéva.
eng_text: Stars give off light and heat because of the energy made when hydrogen atoms are merged (or fused) together to form heavier elements.

text: Umi tembikuaahára omba’apo hína omoheñói hag̃ua peteĩ reactor ikatúva ojapo energía upeichaguaiténte avei.
eng_text: Scientists are working to create a reactor that can make energy in the same way.

text: Hakatu, kóva ha’e peteĩ apañuãi hasyetereíva iñemyatyrõ ha ohasáta heta ary gueteri jahechamboyve ojejapóramo peteĩ fusión rehegua reactor ojeporukuaáva hekopete.
eng_text: This, however, is a very hard problem to solve and will take many years before we see useful fusion reactors built.

text: Acero-guigua ju ovevúi y’ári tensión superficial rupive.
eng_text: The steel needle floats on top of the water because of surface tension.

text: Tensión superficial oiko umi y regua molécula y’áripegua ojoheka mbarete rupi hikuái, hetave umi yvytu molécula hi’ariguápe.
eng_text: Surface tension happens because the water molecules at the surface of the water are strongly attracted to each other more than they are to the air molecules above them.

text: Y molécula ojapo peteĩ pire ojekuaa’ỹva y’ári ha upéva rupi ju ovevúi y’ári.
eng_text: The water molecules make an invisible skin on the water’s surface that allows things like the needle to float on top of the water.

text: Peteĩ yrypy’apegua patín ko’ag̃aguáva oguereko peteĩ ikuaha ojoapytépe. Upéicha rupi mokõive hembe’y ojaporãve yrypy’a rehe, jepéramo oĩ karẽ.
eng_text: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: Upe cuchilla yvypegua ikarẽ rupi michĩmĩ, upe cuchilla ikarẽ’imívo peteĩ térã ambue tenda gotyo, upe hembe’y ojáva yrypyy’áre ikarẽ’imi avei.
eng_text: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: Kóicha rupi patinador ikatu ojere. Upe patín ikarẽramo akatúa gotyo, patinador ojere akatúa gotyo, patín ikarẽramo asu gotyo, patinador ojere ijasu gotyo.
eng_text: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Eho jey hag̃uã energía ojeguereko va’ekuépe, oñemboyke raẽ va’erã energía extra oñeguenohẽ va’ekue luzgui.
eng_text: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: Ojejapo oñeme’ẽnguévo michĩmi luz partícula hérava “fotón”.
eng_text: They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a "photon".

text: Tembikuaarekahára ohenói ko tembiapópe “radiación ñeme’ẽ” umi átomo oñemomỹi rupi luz mimbi rupive, ha omoheñói peteĩ luz fotón rehegua, ha upe luz ha’e peteĩ radiación.
eng_text: Scientists call this process "stimulated emission of radiation" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation.

text: Ambue ta’ãnga ohechauka átomo-kuéra ome’ẽnguévo fotón-kuéra. Añetehápe umi fotón michĩeteve ko ta’ãngapeguápe.
eng_text: The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture.

text: Fotón-kuéra katu michĩve jey umi materia omoñepyrũva átomo-gui!
eng_text: Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!

text: Hetaiterei aravo oiko rire, upe foco filamento okái ha ndoikovéi
eng_text: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works.

text: Ko’agKo’ag̃a katu, emoambueva’erã upe foco. Eñangarekova’erã foco emoambue aja.
eng_text: The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb.

text: Ñepyrũrã, embogue ra’ẽva’erã foco rehegua llave térã emboguete
eng_text: First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected.

text: Kóva oiko upe electricidad oĩva casquillo gotyo oĩháme foco metal uguerekóva ikatu ojapo peteĩ descarga ivaíva ojepokóramo casquillo ryepýpe terã base metálica, oĩ’aja gueteri casquillo-pe.
eng_text: This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.

text: Upe órgano ha’evéva retepy jeikoparãverã  ha’e hína korasõ , omomỹi katui tuguýpe.
eng_text: The major organ of the circulatory system is the heart, which pumps the blood.

text: Tuguy osẽ korasõgui peteĩ tuguy rapére hérava arteria ha ohojey korasõ me ambue ruguy rape hérava vena-kuéra rupive. Umi tuguy rape michĩvéva hérava capilares.
eng_text: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

text: Triceratops raĩnguéra ikaturaka’e ombochipe ndaha’éi togue año, avei hakã ha yvyra rapo hatãvéve.
eng_text: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots.

text: Oĩ tembikuaahára oimo’ãva Triceratops ho’uha cícadas, ha’éva yvyramáta oĩvavoi Cretásico ryepýpe.
eng_text: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

text: Ko yvyramáta ha’ete peteĩ palmera michĩva oguerekóva hogue akua ha haimbéva.
eng_text: These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves.

text: Peteĩ Triceratops ikatu raka'e oipuru pico oguerekóva oipo'o hag̃ua hoguekue ho'umboyve hakãngue.
eng_text: A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk.

text: Oĩ avei tembikuaahára he’íva ko’ã yvyramáta oguerekoha veneno ha upéva rupi ndaipóri dinosaurio ho’uva’erã, hakatu ambue ko’agã rupi perezoso ha ambue mymba gua’áichagua ( dinosaurio descendiente) ikatu ho’u yvyramáta rogué térã yva oguerekóva veneno.
eng_text: Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.

text: Mba’éichapa eguerohorýta ra’e Io gravedad? Eiméramo Io superficie-pe, ndevevuivéta yvypeguágui.
eng_text: How would Io's gravity pull on me? If you stood on the surface of Io, you would weigh less than you do on Earth.

text: Peteĩ tapicha oguerkóva 90 kg yvy’ape’ári, oguerekóta 16 kg rupi Io-pe. Upéicharamo, gravedad, jaikuaaháicha, nembovevuive.
eng_text: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: Kuarahy ndoguerekói peteĩ ape ikatuhápe eñembo’y yvypeguáicha. Kuarahy tuichakue javeve ojejepo gas, tata ha plasma-gui.
eng_text: The Sun doesn't have a crust like the Earth that you can stand on. The whole Sun is made out of gases, fire, and plasma.

text: Gas ipo’ive ohóvo oñemomombyryvévo kuarahy mbytégui.
eng_text: The gas becomes thinner as you go farther from the center of the Sun.

text: Kuarahýre jahecháva ñamañávo hese héra fotosfera, he’iséva “Tata rendy apu’a”.
eng_text: The outer-part we see when we look at the Sun is called the photosphere, which means "ball of light".

text: Ojapo mbohapysu rire rupi, 1610-pe. Italia-pegua astrónomo Galileo Galilei oipuru peteĩ telescopio ohecha hag̃uã Venus oguerekoha fase, jasýicha avei.
eng_text: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: Umi fase-kuéra oiko ojehesape rupi Venus gotyo añónte (térã jasy) omañáva kuarahy gotyo. Umi Venus fase-kuéra oykeko Copérnico remimo’ã he’íva umi planeta-kuéra ojereha kuarahy rehe.
eng_text: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Upéi, heta ary ohasa rire, 1639-pe peteĩ astrónomo inglés hérava Jeremiah Horrocks, ohechakuaa peteĩ Venus rape."
eng_text: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

text: Inglaterra ohasa heta ára py'aguapýpe ojagarra rire pe Danelaw.
eng_text: England had experienced a long period of peace after the reconquest of the Danelaw.

text: Ha 991 arýpe, Ethelred embohovake Vikingo kanoa aty ndive tuichaveva araka’eve ojehecha’ỹva Guthrum mba'éva oiko vaekue 100 ary mboyvégui.
eng_text: However in 991 Ethelred was faced with a Viking fleet larger than any since Guthrum's a century earlier.

text: Upe yga'aty omotenondékuri Olaf Trygvasson, peteĩ Noruego oipotajeýva hetã umi Danés poguýgui.
eng_text: This fleet was led by Olaf Trygvasson, a Norwegian with ambitions to reclaim his country from Danish domination.

text: Osẽ vai ñepyrũvo imilitarkuéra, Ethelred oheka jeiko porã Olaf ndive, ha oho jevy Noruégape ojagarra haguã tetã ha ndaha'éi osẽ porãitéva.
eng_text: After initial military setbacks, Ethelred was able to agree to terms with Olaf, who returned to Norway to try to gain his kingdom with mixed success.

text: Hangeul ha’e achegety oñemoheñóiva jeporu katuirã opavépe guarãva. Ko achegety oñemoheñói 1444-pe rey Sejong reinado jave (1418-1450).
eng_text: Hangeul is the only purposely invented alphabet in popular daily use. The alphabet was invented in 1444 during the reign of King Sejong (1418 – 1450).

text: Rey Sejong ha’e Kuri irundyha rey Joseon dinastía-pegua ha ha’e oñemomba’eguasuvéva.
eng_text: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and is one of the most highly regarded.

text: Ñepyrũraite oñehenói achegety Hangeul Hunmin Jeongeum he’iséva “ Tyapu oĩporãva avakuéra ñemoarandurã”
eng_text: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: Oĩ heta teoría mba’éichapa heñói ra’e sánscrito. Peteĩva he’i oikohague peteĩ migració aria oeste guivo India gotyo ha ogueru iñe’ẽ hendivekuéra.
eng_text: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

text: Sánscrito ha’e peteĩ ñe’ẽ ymaguare ha oñembojoja latín reh oñeñe’ẽva Europa-pe.
eng_text: Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe.

text: Peteĩha aranduka ñepyrũ ojekuaáva yvy ape ári ojehaiva’ekue sánscrito-pe. Upéi Upanishads oñembyaty rire, sánscrito okañyrei jerarquía rupive.
eng_text: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: Sánscrito ha’e peteĩ ñe’ẽ oguerekopaitéva, ojeporúva heta indio moderno ñe’ẽ ñepyrurã, ha latín ha’eháicha avei, ha’e Europa-gua ñe’ẽnguéra taha’e francés térã español.
eng_text: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: Opakuévo ñorãirõ Francia-rupive, Alemania oñepyrũ oñembosako’i oike hag̃ua mbaretépe Gran Bretaña-pe.
eng_text: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: Alemania ombohéra ijeroike "Operación Sealion". Opaite umi arma ipohýiva ha ñorãirõrã tembiporukuéra ejército británico mba’éva okañymba osẽnguévo hikuái Dunkerque-gui, upévagui ko ejército ikangyeterei.
eng_text: Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak.

text: Hakatu Royal Navy imbareteve gueteri ("Kriegsmarine") alemán-gui ha ikatu ombokapu oimeraẽve ygarata oikéva Canal de la Mancha rupive.
eng_text: But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel.

text: Hakatu, sa’ieterei ygarata Royal Navy mba’éva oguereko heda tee umi tape ikatuhárupi ojeike, almirante-kuéra okyhyje rupi ombokapúramog̃uarãhi’arikuéra alemán-kuéra mba’yruveve.
eng_text: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: Ñañepyrũ jaikuaávo mba’épa Italia ojapose ra’e. Italia ha’e upéramo Alemania ha Japón “kyvy”.
eng_text: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: Oguerekova’ekue peteĩ ejército ha ygarata ikangyvéva, jepéramo ojapo ramoite hikuái irundy ygarata pyahu ñorãirõ guasu oñepyrũ mboyve.
eng_text: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: Italia ohupytyse umi Africa-pegua tetãnguéra. Ojapyhy hag̃uã umi tetãnguéra oguerekova’erã peteĩ plataforma tropa-kuéra, ikatuhag̃uãicha oike Mar Mediterráneo rupive ha ohekojopy Africa-pe.
eng_text: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: Upevarã, ohejareiva’erã hikuái umi base ha ygarata británico Egipto-pe. Avei upéva ári, umi ygarata italiano ndojapoveímiva’erã mba’eve.
eng_text: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: "Ko’agã Japón-peguarã. Japón ha’eva’ekue peteĩ tetã insular, ha’eháicha Gran Bretaña."
eng_text: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: Umi submarino hína ygarata ojejapova'ekue oiko hag̃ua oñapymĩhápe ha oikokuaa upéicha heta arange peve.
eng_text: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: Submarino-kuéra ojeporuva’ekue Peteĩha Ñorãirõ Guasu ha mokõiha Ñorãirõ Guasu Yvy’ape’ariguápe. Upéramo guare imbegue gueteri hikuái ha nombokapúi gueteri mombyry.
eng_text: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: Ñorãirõ ñepyrũme, opavave submarino oikundaha ysyry guasu ári, hakatu radar oñembokatypyryvépe, umi submarino-kuéra oñapymĩma ojehecha’ỹhag̃uãicha.
eng_text: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: Umi submarino alemán héra U-Boats. Alemán-kuéra ikatupyry ygaratápe jeiko ha submarino jeporúpe.
eng_text: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: Oipurukuaa rupi hikuái umi submarino, ñorãirõ opa rire, oje’émi va'ekue Alemania-gua ndoguerekóiha heta submarino.
eng_text: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Upeichaite! Rey Tutankamón, sapy’ánte ojeheróva “Rey Tut” térã “ Rey mitã’iva”, ha’e rey itujavéva Egipto-pe, ojekuaavéva ko’ag̃a rupi.
eng_text: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: Jaikuaahag̃uãnte, noñemomba’eguasúi chupe ymaitevéramo ha noñemboguapýi héra umi rey-kuéra réra rysýi ymave guarépe.
eng_text: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Hakatu, he’õngue renda jejuhu 1922-pe, omomba’eguasueteri ichupe. Heta te’õngue renda ymaguaréva oñemonda, kóva katu ojejuhu aimete oĩhaguéichaite.
eng_text: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: Aimete tembiporukuéra oñeñotyva’ekue Tutankhamon-ndive, ojejuhu porãiterei, oĩhápe hetaiterei tembiporu ojejapopyre metal-gui ha ita ojehecha’ỹva.
eng_text: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: Umi rueda ñemoheñói rupive mba’yrumỹi asirio-va ivevúi ha ipya’eve ha ohejakuaáma tapykuépe soldado-kuéra ha ambue mba’yrumỹi oĩvape.
eng_text: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Hu’ykuéra oipurúva ikatu ombokua umi armadura oipurúva oñorairõva hendivekuéra. Ary 1000 a.C.,- kuérape rupi umi asirio ogueroikéma kavaju jeporu ñorairõhápe.
eng_text: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: Caballería ha’e peteĩ ejército oñorairõva kavaju ári. Hakatu ndoguerekói gueteri ikalcha jeguapyrã, upévare caballería asiria oñorairõ kavaju nandi ári gueteri.
eng_text: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Roikuaa heta político-pe, tembiakuaahára ha tembiapojeguahára griego-va. Umiva apytépe ojekuaavéva ikatu hína Homero, ñe’ẽpapahára griego, ohaiva’ekue jehaipyporãmby mba’eguasuetéva: Ñe’ẽpoty Ilíada ha Odisea.
eng_text: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: Sófocles ha Aristófanes ha’e gueteri ñe’ẽpapahára popular ha hembiapokuéra oñemomba’eguasu yvy’ape’árigua jehaiporãmby iporãvéva.
eng_text: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Avei ambue grigo ojehecharamovéva ha’e matemático Pitágoras, ojekuavéva omoheñói rehe teorema umi triángulo rectángulo rehegua.
eng_text: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: Hetaichagua ñeimo’ã oĩ avakuéra oñe’ẽva hindi rehe. Oje’etemi oĩha mokõiha ha Irundyha ñe’ẽ apytépe oñeñe’ẽvéva yvy ape ári.
eng_text: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: Ñe’ẽharaitévavoi iñambuekuaa ojehecháramo umi dialecto ojoajuetereíva ojuehe.
eng_text: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Umíva apytépe jajuhukuaa 340 millón ha 500 millón ñe’ẽharakuéra, ha 800 millón avakuéra rupi ikatu oikumbu ko ñe’ẽ.
eng_text: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: Hindi ha urdu ojojogua hikuái ñe’ẽavúpe hakatu ndaupéichai ijehaípe; ñomongeta katuípe ikatu ojokupytypa oñondivekuéra.
eng_text: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: Siglo XV mbytérupi, Estonia norte-gua, oĩva’ekue Alemania arandupyeta poguýpe.
eng_text: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: Oĩ umi monje alemán-kuéra omo’ãguiséva Ñandejára umi indígena-kuéra rehe, upévarã omoheñói hikuái estonio ñe’ẽ.
eng_text: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: Oñemopyenda alemán achegety rehe ha oñemoĩ tai “Õ / õ”.
eng_text: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: Ohasavo arange, heta ñe’ẽnguéra ojeporu alemán-gui ha ojoaju ojuehe. Upéicha oñepyrũ iluminación.
eng_text: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: Ojejapova’erãháicha, trono-pegua heredero ohova’erã ejército-pe mbo’ehao omohu’ã riremínte.
eng_text: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Hakatu Charles oho Trinity College Mbo’ehaovusúpe, Cambridge, upépe oñemoarandu Antropología ha Arqueología-pe ha uperire Historia, ohupytyhápe3 2:2 ( jehechakuaa mokõihápegua)
eng_text: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Charles  ha’e Kuri Familia Real Británica apytégui ohupytýva peteĩ título mbo’ehaovusúpe.
eng_text: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: Turquía Europa-gua (Tracia oriental o Rumelia en la península de los Balcanes) ojeroike 3% tetãgui.
eng_text: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Turquía yvy oguereko hetave 1.600 kilómetros (1.000 millas) ipukukue ha 800 km (500 millas) ipekue.
eng_text: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Turquía retepy, taha’e yno’õ, oipuru 783,562 kilómetros cuadrados (300,948 millas cuadradas),upévagui 755,688 kilómetros cuadrados (291,773 millas cuadradas) ojejuhu Asia suroeste gotyo ha 23,764 kilómetros cuadrados (9,174 millas cuadradas) oĩ Europa-pe.
eng_text: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Turquía retepy ojapo ichugui 37 hápe tetã tuichavéva yvy’ape’ári ha oguereko Francia metropolitana ha  Reino Unido oñondive tuichakue rupi.
eng_text: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Turquía rehe ojere ysyry gausu mbohapyve tenda gotyo: Egeo oĩ oeste gotyo, Negro oĩ norte gotyo ha Mediterraneo oĩ sur gotyo.
eng_text: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: Luxemburgo hembiasa pukúma, katu isãso 1839 ary guiveramo.
eng_text: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Belgica yvy pehẽ kko’agãgua ymave Luxemburgo yvy va’ekue, katu ohasa Bélgica poguýpe Revolución belga 1830 rire.
eng_text: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Luxemburgo akói oñeha’ã oiko hag̃ua tetã oñemombytéva apañuãime ramo, katu Ñorãirõ Guasu Peteĩ ha Mokõihápe oike Alemania poguýpe.
eng_text: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: Ary 1957-pe, Luxemburgo oĩ atyvete ojeheróva Unión Europea omoñepyrũva apytépe.
eng_text: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Drukgyal Dzong ningo peteĩ fortaleza tapere ha peteĩ monasterio budista oĩva yvate Paro distrito-pe (Phondey Village-pe).
eng_text: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Oje’e 1649 ramo, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel omoñepyrũ peteĩ fortaleza omomorã hag̃ua osẽre tenonde ñorãirõhára tibetano-mongoles rovake.
eng_text: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: Ary 1951 ramo, tata guasu rupive opyta sa’imíntema Drukgyal Dzong reliquia, umíva apytépe Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal ra’ãnga.
eng_text: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Tata guasu rire, oñeñangareko pe fortaleza rehe, oikóvo chugui peteĩva umi mba’e ojehechasevéva Bután-pe.
eng_text: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: Siglo XVIII aja, Camboya ojejopynunga mokõi ijykepegua ipokatuvéva mbytépe, Tailandia ha Vietnam.
eng_text: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: Tailandi-gua oike Camboya yvýpe heta jey siglo XVIII aja ha 1772-pe ohundiete Phnom Phen.
eng_text: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: Umi arypaha siglo XVIII ryepýpe, Vietnan-gua avei oike Camboya yvýpe.
eng_text: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Dieciocho por ciento Venezuela-gua rupi oĩ hembiapo’ỹva ha hetaiteve umi hembiapóva apytépe omba’apo economía informal-pe.
eng_text: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: Dos tercio umi Venezuela-gua hembiapóva apytépe oñemongu’e sector servicio-pe, haimete peteĩ cuarta parte omba’apo industria-pe ha quinta parte agricultura-pe.
eng_text: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Industria tuichavéva Venezuela-guápe g̃uarã hína petróleo, tetã oĩhápe exportador tuichávaramo, jepérõ upéicha uno por ciento añónte omba’apoindistria petrolera-pe.
eng_text: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Tetã isãso ypýrõ guare, umi Jardín Botánico apo Singapúr-pe oipytyvõ pe isla-gui oiko hag̃ua peteĩ Ciudad Jardín tropical.
eng_text: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: 1981 arýpe, Vanda Miss Joaquim,  híbrido de orquídeas, ojeiporavo tetã yvotýramo.
eng_text: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: Opa ary oguahẽvape, jasypa rupi, amo 1,5 millones mymba ka’avo’uha oho sur gotyo umi llanura-pe, ohasávo río Mara, colina norte-pegua guive okyeteri rupi.
eng_text: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Ha upéi ojevy jey norte gotyo oeste guio, ohasa jeývo río Mara, okypa rire jasyrundy rupi.
eng_text: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Serengeti región oreko Parque Nacional de Serengeti, peteĩ  Ngorongoro  Área de Conservación ha Reserva de Caza Maswa Tanzania-pe ha Reserva Nacional de Maasai Mara Kenia-pe.
eng_text: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Medio interactivo apokuaarã tekotevẽ aporeko ojeikuaa ha ojeiporu akóiva, upéichaavei ojeguereko va’erã pojoapy ojeporukuaáva umi clase interactivo-pe (storyboard, ñehendurã ha ta’ãngamýi ñemohenda, tembiasañemombe’u ha ambue)
eng_text: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Diseño interactivo oikotevẽ ejesareko jey neremimo’ã paha producción de medio rehegua rehe ha ejepokuaa ani eñamindu’u peteĩ hendáichante.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: Diseño interactivo oikotevẽ umi componentepeteĩ apopyrãmegua tojoaju oñondivepa, katuavei tahi’añete peteĩ teĩ ha’ekuera haichaite.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Desventaja ojejuhúva umi objetivo zoom reheveguápe ningo hína pe complejidad focal elementos objetivo reheguaretakue,  tekotevẽva ojehupyty hag̃ua peteĩ rango de distancias focales hetaiteve umi objetivo fijo-pe g̃uarãva rovake.
eng_text: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: Kóvagui oiko apañuãi tuichaite’ỹmava umi lente apoha ojuhu rupiestándar ijyvatevévalente apópe.
eng_text: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: Kóva rupive umi obejtivo zoom rehevegua toguenohẽ ta’ãnga iporãngue ikatútava oñembojoja umi ta’ãnga oñeguenohẽva objetivo oiporúva distancia focal fija rupive rehe.
eng_text: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: Ambue desventaja orekóva lente zoom rehevegua hína pe apertura máxima (ipya’ekue) michĩve jepi.
eng_text: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: Kóva rupive umi objetivo zoom hepete’ỹva jeporu hasyve jepi hesakãpora’ỹhápe flash’ỹre.
eng_text: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Peteĩ mba'e hasyvéva akói oñembohasa haguã ta'ãngamýi DVD-pe hina pe ijykekuéra ñeikytĩ.
eng_text: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: Umi ta'angambyrykuéra ojejapo ombovy'a haguã ambue avakuérape.
eng_text: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: Upévare, opa mba'e rehecháva pe ta'angambyry pe oñekytĩ pe ijere, yvate, yvy gotyo ha ijykepe.
eng_text: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: Péva ojejapo hina ikatuhag̃uáicha pe ta'anga ryrýi ojagarrapa pe pantalla. Péva ojehero hina ijykekuéra ñeikytĩ.
eng_text: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: Upeicha avei, ejaporõ pe DVD, ijyke kuera oñeikytĩ avei, ha pe video oguerekorõ taí kuéra pe ivype, ndaikatumo'ai ojehecha porã.
eng_text: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Umi castillo medieval ymaguare ymaiteguive oinspira umi py'amongeta, omomagiavo umi caballero kuéra, karu guasu ha caballeria Arturo ara peguare.
eng_text: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Umi óga guasu rembyre su ary oguerekóva apytépe ndahasýi jagueru hag̃ua ñane akãme umi tyapu ha ty'akuã umi ñorãirõ oikova'ekue, ha avei ñahendúvaicha umi kavaju py ryapu tapehũ rehe ha ñahetũ pe kyhyje ry'akuã osẽva mazmorra guive.
eng_text: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: Jepe jajepyʼamongeta osẽ umi ñande rembiasagui? Mba'ere ojejapo raka'e umi tavetã roga guasu kuéra? Mba'éichapa ra'e oje diseña ha oñemopu'ã?
eng_text: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: Yma guareichaite, Kirby Muxloe castillo ojoguave peteĩ hóga oñeñangareko hatãva peteĩ castillo tee rãngue.
eng_text: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Hovetã tuichaicha cristal reheve ha hogyke pererĩ ndaikatumo’ãi kuri ombohovake are peteĩ ataque.
eng_text: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: 1480 década-pe, Lord Hasting oñepyrũramo guare omopu’ã, ko tetã oiko va’ekue py’aguapýpe nunga ha tekotevẽ va’ekue oñeñangareko tapicha rekovai sapy’agua aty’i mimi rehe añónte.
eng_text: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Pokatu ñembojoja ningo va’ekue peteĩ sistema tetã Europa-gua oiporúva oheka hag̃ua soberanía nacional jeguereko opaite umi tetã Europa-guápe.
eng_text: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Ko’ápe ojeheka va’ekue hína opaite tetã Europa-gua toñepia’ã ani hag̃ua peteĩ tetãnte jepeve ohupyty pokatu, ha upévare, tetã rekuaikuéra akoiete omoambuéva iñirũ ani hag̃ua mba’eve oiko hendape’ỹ.
eng_text: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Pe Guerra de Sucesión española omoñepyrũ peteĩha ñorairõ ha upépe ojeheka va'ekue pe pokatu rekojoja.
eng_text: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: Kóva omoambue peteĩ mba’e tuichaitereíva, umi Eropape ipokatuvéva ndaikatuvéitama rupi oreko mba’érepa omongu’éta ñorãirõ jeroviapy rehe. Upevare, pe Guerra de los Treinta Años ha’éta pe ipahapegua ojeherótava ñorãirõ jeroviapy rehe.
eng_text: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: Artemisa templo oĩva Éfeso-pe oñehundi va’ekue 21 jasypokõi 356 a.C. arýpe tarendy Herostrato omoñepyrũvape.
eng_text: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: Hembiasakue omombe’uháicha, fama jehupyty oimeháicha pe mba’e omongyre’ỹve va’ekue chupe. Efesio-kuéra, pochýre, he’i va’ekue Hrostratus réra araka’eve ndohechamo’ãiha upéva.
eng_text: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: Tembiasa haiha Grecia-gua Estrabón ohai tenondeve, ha’eha ko árape ojeikuaaháicha. Pe templo ojeitypa va’ekue pyhare Alejandro Magno heñóiramo guare.
eng_text: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Alejandro, rey-ramo, oikuave’ẽ pe templo ñemopu’ã repy jehepyme’ẽ, katu oñembotove chupe. Uperire, Alejandro omano rire, pe templo oñemopu’ã jey 323 a.C. arýpe.
eng_text: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Eñeha’ãke nde po topytu’u porã ikatuháicha epove aja ehóvo umi nota hekoitépe; eñeha’ã avei ani emongu’evai ne kuã.
eng_text: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Upéicha sa’ive nekane’õta. Nemandu’áke natekotevẽiha ejopy hatãiterei umi tecla embopu hatãve hag̃ua piano-pe tekotevẽháicha.
eng_text: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Acordeón-pe, oñembopu hatãve hag̃ua ojejopy hatã térã pya’eve fuelle.
eng_text: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Pe misticismo ningo hína comunión, identidad térã conocimiento consciente peteĩ realidad ultima, divinidad, angapy añete térã Dios jeheka.
eng_text: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Pe creyente oheka peteĩ experiencia directa, realidad divina térã umi deidad jeju térã ijehechakuaa.
eng_text: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Ohapykuehóva oheka peteĩ hendaicha ojeikove hag̃ua térã mba’e ojejapokuaáva oñemombareteve hag̃ua umi tembiasa.
eng_text: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: Misticismo ikatu ojehecha ambue hendaichagua jeroviapy ha iñemomorãramo omomba’eve rehe pe experiencia personal ojeguerekóva peteĩ estado de conciencia ipeteĩva rehe, ko’ýte umi heko py’aguapyvéva, hembihechakuaa, ivy’a pypukukuaáva rehe.
eng_text: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Sijismo ningo peteĩ jeroviapy subcontinente indio-pegua.  Oñepyrũ Punjab región-pe siglo XV ramo tradición indu oñemboja’o rire.
eng_text: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Sijs-kuérape g̃uarã ijeroviapy ndaha’éi peteĩ hinduismo pehẽ, jepéramo he’i avei upégui ouhague hikuái.
eng_text: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Sijs-kuéra ohero ijeroviapy Gurmat-ramo, punjabi ñe’ẽme he’iséva “gurú rape”. Gurú ningo peteĩ teko oñeikotevẽtereíva India-pegua jeroviapykuérape g̃uarã, katu sijismo-pe ojeguereko pe mba’e omopyendáva sij jeroviapýramo.
eng_text: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: Ko jeroviapyomoñepyrũ va’ekue Guru Nanak siglo XV-ramo (1469-1539). Ha’e rire ou porundy ambue gurú ojoapykuéri.
eng_text: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Upéicharõ jepe, jasypoteĩ 1956 ramo, Krushchev promesa-kuéra oñeha’ã Polonia-pe oĩrõ guare mba’apoharakuéra oguerosapukáiva hesa’ipa rupi hi’upyrã ha tembiapo repy oñemboguejy rupi, upévagui upéi oñepyrũ peteĩ trotesta general comunismo rovake.
eng_text: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Jepéramo ipahápe Krushchev oguerahauka tanque ojoko hag̃ua sarambi, omonĩ upépe ojejeruréva ha oñemoĩ peteĩ ñe’ẽme omohenda hag̃ua Wladyslaw Gomulka ojehayhúvape primer ministro ramo.
eng_text: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Valle del Indo-pegua civilización ningo ou Edad de Bronce-gui, India noreste-pegua subcontinente ko’ág̃a oĩha Pakistán tuichakue nunga ha michĩmi India ha Afganistán noreste.
eng_text: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: Ko civilización okakuaa río Indo pukukue, upégui ou héra.
eng_text: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Jepéramo oĩ tapicha arandu he’íva pe civilizción oĩ rupi avei río Sarasvati syry, ko’ág̃a opáma pukuke, añetehápe ojehero va’erã kuri civilizción Indo-Sarasvati, oĩ aja ambue ohenóiva chupe civilización Harappa, upeicha héra rupi tenda ojejo’o ypyhague 1920 década-pe.
eng_text: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Imperio romano reko militarista rehe oipytyvõ ojeguerojera haguã ñepohãnokuéra.
eng_text: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: Pohãnoharakuéra oike ñepyrũ recluta-ramo emperador Augusto rupi ha avei oĩ Cuerpo Medico Roma-gua tenondetévape, ojeiporu haguã chupekuéra ñorairo rire.
eng_text: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: Cirujano-kuéra oikuaa va'ekue heta sedante, oĩ avei pype morfina oñeguenohẽva amapola ra'ỹigui ha escopolamina herbano ra'ỹigui.
eng_text: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: Ojapokuaa hikuái amputación oñangareko haguã paciente-kuérape gangrena-gui, ha avei torniquete apo ha pinza arterial-kuéra ojoko haguã tyguy rape.
eng_text: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: h-eta siglo aja, imperio Roma-gua ombohape heta mba'e jeguereko medicina-pe ha ojekuaa heta mba'e jaikuaáva ko'ã árape.
eng_text: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Origami yvy tee hína origami ijapýrava ojejapokuaáva peteĩ pliegue año ohóvo, ndojehejai pliegue hasyvéva apo, pliegue ypy gotyoguáicha, ha opa pliegue oguereko tenda ndahasýiva.
eng_text: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: Ojapo va'ekue Jonh Smith 1970 década-pe oipytyvõ haguã carpeta hembiasa'ỹva térã omyikuaa porã'ỹvape.
eng_text: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Mitãnguéra oguerojera peteĩ raza rehegua conciencia ha estereotipo raza rehegua imitã guive ha ko'ã estereotipo opoko compotamiento oguerekóva rehe.
eng_text: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Techapyrã, mitanguéra oikuaáva peteĩ raza sa'ivevaguaha orekóva estereotipo ndoikoiha mbo'ehaópe, ndoikói jepi mbo'ehaópe ágã oikuaa rire oje'éva heseguakuéra rehe.
eng_text: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: MySpace hína mbohapyha web renda ojehecharamovéva ojeiporúva Estados Unidos-pe ha ogureko 54 millon perfil hina ko'agãite.
eng_text: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Ko'ã pagina internet pegua kuéra oreko heta jesareko, ha hetave upe tekombo'e apytepe.
eng_text: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: Ko pagina internet oguereko heta mba'e porã, umia ha'e hina, ikatu embosako'i nde tekombo'e página kuéra ha'eva hina jehaipyre, ta'anga ryryi, ta'anga kuéra ha heta ambue mba'e.
eng_text: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.
